core_obligations: Choose an injective embedding (proof lines 16907-16910): take 0 -> F -> I -> Q -> 0 with I an injective sheaf of Z/nZ-modules, and consider the displayed diagram whose rows are the long exact cohomology sequences of the two rows, the zero in the upper right corner coming from injectivity of I.

Use the hypothesis (proof lines 16911-16919): the two left vertical arrows are isomorphisms by BC(f, n, q-1), so the map (f')^{-1}R^q g_*F -> R^q h_*e^{-1}F is injective, which is part (1); moreover the cokernel of that map embeds into R^q h_*e^{-1}I, which is part (3).

Get part (2) (proof lines 16920-16936): given F subset G with G annihilated by n, choose F subset G subset I and compare the two cokernels inside R^q h_*e^{-1}I, so that the cokernel for F is contained in that for G.
proof_roadmap: Embed the coefficient sheaf into an injective Z/nZ-module and write the two long exact sequences as a diagram.
Read injectivity and the embedding of the cokernel into R^q h_* of the injective off the diagram, using BC(f, n, q-1) for the two left arrows.
Refine the embedding to F subset G subset I to compare the two cokernels, giving part (2).
difficulty_reason: The lemma extracts three consequences for the q-th base change map from the hypothesis BC(f, n, q-1) (statement lines 16868-16904). The proof (proof lines 16906-16936) embeds the coefficient sheaf into an injective Z/nZ-module, arranges the two long exact sequences in one diagram, uses the assumed isomorphisms in degree q-1 for the left vertical arrows to obtain injectivity and the embedding of the cokernel, and refines the embedding to compare cokernels for part (2). H2: one diagram chase with an explicit injective embedding, written out.
